workedExample: The complement theorem gives NL equals coNL. Savitch gives PSPACE equals NPSPACE. Reingold gives deterministic logarithmic space for undirected reachability. These space results do not settle deterministic versus nondeterministic log space or the time-class question NP versus coNP.

Correct. 2-SAT unsatisfiability reduces to reachability (a path from x to not-x and from not-x back to x in the implication graph), so it's in NL; since NL equals coNL, 2-SAT satisfiability is in NL too.

workedExample: At logarithmic space the complement theorem gives NL equals coNL, so directed unreachability is also in NL. At linear space it gives complement closure for context-sensitive languages, with the usual empty-word convention. An inconsistent 2-SAT implication cycle can be guessed in log space; complement closure handles satisfiability too. None of this proves the time analogue NP equals coNP or L equals NL.
